newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down in quiet market.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices lost their early stability to end down after the market drifted without buying interest the whole day, traders said.
"It was quiet through the day and it was not surprising that the prices were down again," said a trader.
At the close, the MRELB quoted February RSS1 buyer at 303.50 cents ($1.22) a kg, unchanged from Wednesday's close. February SMR20 was also half cent down at 300 cents.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 301 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 369, SMR L at 350, SMR 10 at 302 and drum latex FOB at 236.

Traders said some buying interest could be seen after the Eid al-Fitr and Chinese New Year holidays in mid-February, when plantations stop tapping rubber for nearly a week and put a strain on supply of latex to the market.
The INRO five-day average was at 236.08 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 15 from 236.86 on Jan 14. The daily indicator was 234.90 against 238.86 previously.
